statement: Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, the following holds. Let n = len(nums) and m = n/2. For a length-n sequence b of integers, call b admissible when 0 <= b[i] <= k for every i with 0 <= i < n and there exists an integer X with 0 <= X <= k such that |b[j] - b[n-1-j]| = X for every j with 0 <= j < m. Let changes(b) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and b[i] != nums[i]. Then r is the minimum value of changes(b) over all admissible b; equivalently, there exists an admissible b with changes(b) = r and every admissible b has changes(b) >= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: The call min_changes nums k returns a result r; in particular it does not fail, overflow, index out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(nums)/2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k, and additionally len(nums) = 2.

statement: Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there exists an integer X with 0 <= X <= k such that for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums)/2, |nums[j] - nums[len(nums)-1-j]| = X.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, r <= the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums)/2 and nums[j] != nums[len(nums)-1-j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: Let n = len(nums), m = n/2, and for each j with 0 <= j < m let D_j = |nums[j] - nums[n-1-j]|. Let F be the maximum, over all integers X with 0 <= X <= k, of the number of j with 0 <= j < m and D_j = X. Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, r >= m - F.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and m = n/2. For each j with 0 <= j < m and each integer X with 0 <= X <= k, let c_j(X) be the least nonnegative integer c for which there exist integers u and v with 0 <= u <= k, 0 <= v <= k, |u-v| = X, and c = (if u != nums[j] then 1 else 0) + (if v != nums[n-1-j] then 1 else 0). Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, for every integer X with 0 <= X <= k we have r <= sum_{j=0}^{m-1} c_j(X).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and m = n/2. For each j with 0 <= j < m and each integer X with 0 <= X <= k, let c_j(X) be the least nonnegative integer c for which there exist integers u and v with 0 <= u <= k, 0 <= v <= k, |u-v| = X, and c = (if u != nums[j] then 1 else 0) + (if v != nums[n-1-j] then 1 else 0). Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, there exists an integer X with 0 <= X <= k such that r = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} c_j(X).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: Let n = len(nums), and let nums' be the sequence of length n defined by nums'[i] = nums[n-1-i] for every i with 0 <= i < n. If min_changes nums k returns a result r and min_changes nums' k returns a result r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and m = n/2. For any sequence nums' of length n such that for every j with 0 <= j < m either (nums'[j] = nums[j] and nums'[n-1-j] = nums[n-1-j]) or (nums'[j] = nums[n-1-j] and nums'[n-1-j] = nums[j]), if min_changes nums k returns a result r and min_changes nums' k returns a result r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.

statement: If min_changes nums k1 returns a result r1 and min_changes nums k2 returns a result r2, then r2 <= r1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000. Let k1 and k2 be 64-bit integers with 0 <= k1 <= k2 <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k1.

statement: Let n = len(nums), m = n/2, and let t be the number of j with 0 <= j < m and nums[j] != nums[n-1-j]. Whenever min_changes nums k returns a result r, r = min(t, m - t).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k, and additionally k = 1.

statement: Let n = len(nums), m = n/2, and let π be any permutation of {0,...,m-1}. Define nums' of length n by nums'[j] = nums[π(j)] and nums'[n-1-j] = nums[n-1-π(j)] for every j with 0 <= j < m. If min_changes nums k returns a result r and min_changes nums' k returns a result r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). nums is a slice of 64-bit integers and k is a 64-bit integer. n is even, 2 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= k.
